notes: Generation codes differ by source: English Wikipedia gives model codes 9YA/9YB and body codes 9Y0 (SUV) and 9Y3 (Coupé); German Wikipedia uses 'Typ PO536'; Porsche uses 'E3'. The slug 'e3' uses Porsche's own designation. All of these are recorded as codes.

Cayenne Coupé: Porsche's press release presenting it is dated 21 March 2019, and it had its exhibition (Asian) premiere at Auto Shanghai in April 2019. English Wikipedia says it 'was revealed during the Shanghai Auto Show in April 2019', which is inconsistent with Porsche's earlier release.
Porsche figures that differ from English Wikipedia: 2017 Cayenne S torque 550 Nm (Porsche) vs 549 Nm (WP table); 2023 Cayenne S 349 kW (474 PS) (Porsche) vs 475 PS (WP).

No complete manufacturer dimensions were readable: Porsche's 2017 and 2023 press kits are PDFs, and the HTML press kit pages give no length, width or height. English Wikipedia gives only ranges (length 4,918–4,929 mm, Coupé 4,931–4,942 mm), so only the wheelbase is recorded. Porsche says the Cayenne Electric is 55 mm longer than the combustion model.
SUV boot volume (770 L per Porsche's 2017 press kit, as seen in a search snippet) could not be read with the project tool and is not recorded.
English Wikipedia says sales began in 2019, which conflicts with the 2017 launch (Porsche held press drives in 2017). This is not recorded. Model years 2019–present are given without a market.

Wikimedia Commons: no 'Category:Porsche Cayenne (9Y0)' exists; 'Category:Porsche Cayenne Coupé (PO536)' exists as a subcategory of 'Category:Porsche Cayenne Coupé'. No generation-level category was confirmed, and none for the 2023 facelift.

It is sold alongside the third-generation combustion and plug-in hybrid Cayenne: Porsche says the Cayenne Electric 'complements the existing offering of combustion-engined and plug-in hybrid Cayenne models', and German Wikipedia says 'Sie wird parallel zum PO536 angeboten'. English Wikipedia notes that a fourth-generation combustion Cayenne has not been confirmed.

Wheelbase: Porsche gives 3,023 mm; English Wikipedia's infobox gives 3,024 mm. Porsche's figure is recorded. Porsche newsroom data refers to the German market (newsroom terms), so it is recorded as EU.

Power figures: the entry model and Turbo are recorded with their Launch Control figures, the S at its normal system output. Normal-mode outputs are 300 kW (Cayenne) and 630 kW (Turbo); the S makes 490 kW with Launch Control.
The 781–1,588 L boot range is stated without the seat positions; the Coupé range is 534 (rear seats in 'cargo' position) to 1,347 L.
Cayenne Electric orders opened at reveal (Porsche: 'available to order now'). The Coupé Electric premiered at Auto China 2026 in Beijing (Porsche release of 24 April 2026).
